# Getting started

## Requirements

* Ruby 3.4 or later, and Rails 7.1 or later.
* [Bootstrap 4](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.6/)'s CSS. The components use its classes, such as `form-control`,
  `dropdown-menu`, `btn` and `spinner-border`.
* [Bootstrap Icons](https://icons.getbootstrap.com/)' CSS, for the icons the components render, such as `bi-x`.
* [Dart Sass](https://sass-lang.com/dart-sass/), if you compile the components' Sass.

## Install the gem

Add the gem to your `Gemfile`:

```rb
gem "impulse_view_components"
```

Then install it:

```bash
bundle install
```

## Require the engine

Require the engine in `config/application.rb`:

```rb
require "impulse/view_components/engine"
```

## Install the JavaScript package

The interactive components ship as custom elements, so you also need the npm package. It's built on
[`@ambiki/impulse`](https://github.com/Ambiki/impulse) 2, which you install alongside it, so your own elements and the
components share one copy:

```bash
yarn add @ambiki/impulse-view-components @ambiki/impulse
```

## Import the components

Each component is imported individually, so you only ship what you use.
For example, to use the [Select](/components/select) component:

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';
```

To register every component at once, import the package itself:

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components';
```

See the **Imports** section on each component's page for the exact paths.

## Import the styles

The styles are written in Sass on top of [Bootstrap 4](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.6/). Load Bootstrap's Sass
functions, variables and mixins first (importing all of `bootstrap` does that), then the base styles once, then each
component's styles:

```scss
@import 'bootstrap/scss/functions';
@import 'bootstrap/scss/variables';
@import 'bootstrap/scss/mixins';

@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/base';
@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';
```

To include every component's styles, import the package itself instead of `base` and each component:

```scss
@import 'bootstrap/scss/functions';
@import 'bootstrap/scss/variables';
@import 'bootstrap/scss/mixins';

@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components';
```

These paths work through webpack's `sass-loader` and Vite. When you run the `sass` command line directly, as
`cssbundling-rails` does, prefix each path with `pkg:` and pass `--pkg-importer=node`, which needs Dart Sass 1.71 or
later:

```scss
@import 'pkg:@ambiki/impulse-view-components/base';
@import 'pkg:@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';
```

A setup that only passes `--load-path=node_modules` can't read these paths, because it looks for files rather than
reading the package's `exports`. It can keep importing the files directly:

```scss
@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/dist/styles/variables';
@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/dist/styles/base';
@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/dist/elements/autocomplete';
```

### Without Sass

If your app doesn't compile Sass, import the precompiled CSS, which holds every component's styles:

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/styles.css';
```

It's built with Bootstrap's default variables, and doesn't include Bootstrap's component CSS, which you still load. Change
colors and sizes through the CSS custom properties it defines
on `:root`, such as `--awc-autocomplete-control-min-height`.

## Upgrading from `dist/` paths

Paths that start with `@ambiki/impulse-view-components/dist/` are deprecated. They keep working, but the docs now
use the shorter paths below.

| Deprecated path                                                  | Use instead                                                                    |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `…/dist/index.js`                                                | `@ambiki/impulse-view-components`                                              |
| `…/dist/elements/<name>`, `…/dist/elements/<name>/index.js`      | `@ambiki/impulse-view-components/<name>`, such as `…/popover`                  |
| `import useFloatingUI from '…/dist/hooks/use_floating_ui'`       | `import { useFloatingUI } from '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/hooks'`        |
| `import useOutsideClick from '…/dist/hooks/use_outside_click'`   | `import { useOutsideClick } from '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/hooks'`      |
| `@import '~…/dist/elements/<name>'`                              | `@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/<name>'`                             |
| `@import '~…/dist/styles/variables'` and `'~…/dist/styles/base'` | `@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/base'`                               |
| Any `…/dist/helpers/*`, or `…/dist/elements/autocomplete/<module>` such as `ajax_search` | None. These modules are internal, and stay reachable only through their `dist/` paths. |

The Sass rows need a setup that reads the package's `exports`. See [Import the styles](#import-the-styles).

Each element path exports its class by name, such as `AwcPopoverElement`, along with the types its properties use.
`…/hooks` exports the types the hooks take and return.

url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/components/ajax-select.md

# Ajax select

Ajax select allows users to fetch a list of options from the server.

## Usage

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::AjaxSelectComponent.new(:post, :person_id, :id, :name, src: "/users")) %>
```

## Arguments

### Positional arguments

| Name         | Default   | Description                                                      |
| ------       | --------- | -------------                                                    |
| object\_name  | N/A       | The name of the object.                                          |
| method\_name  | N/A       | The name of the method.                                          |
| value\_method | N/A       | The method called on the `selected` object to read each option's value (e.g. `:id`).        |
| text\_method  | N/A       | The method called on the `selected` object to read each option's display text (e.g. `:name`). |

### Keyword arguments

| Name              | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                       |
| ------            | --------- | -------------                                                                                                                                     |
| selected          | `nil`     | An object that responds to `value_method` and `text_method`, or an array of them for a `multiple` select.                                         |
| src               | N/A       | The endpoint to fetch the options from.                                                                                                           |
| param             | `"q"`     | The param that is appended when making a network request. Example: `/fruits?q=Guava`.                                                             |
| size              | `:md`     | The size of the select control. One of `:sm`, `:md`, or `:lg`.                                                                                    |
| name              | `nil`     | The name of the field. By default, Rails automatically creates a `name` string based on the `object_name` and `method_name`.                      |
| input\_id          | `nil`     | The id of the input field.                                                                                                                        |
| placeholder       | `nil`     | The placeholder text that is displayed within the input field.                                                                                    |
| include\_hidden    | `true`    | Only applies to a `multiple` select. See the "Gotcha" section of the Rails [`select`](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/FormOptionsHelper.html#method-i-select) tag. |
| disabled          | `false`   | Disables the select control.                                                                                                                      |
| required          | `false`   | Makes the select control a required field.                                                                                                        |
| multiple          | `false`   | Whether multiple values can be selected or not.                                                                                                   |
| clearable         | `true`    | Whether the clear button should be shown or not.                                                                                                  |
| auto\_size         | `true`    | If `true`, caps the listbox's height to the space between it and the edge of the viewport, so a long list scrolls instead of running off screen.  |
| auto\_size\_padding | `4`       | The space in pixels to keep between the listbox and the edge of the viewport when `auto_size` is enabled.                                         |

Any other keyword arguments are passed to the `<awc-autocomplete>` element as HTML attributes, except `namespace`,
`skip_default_ids` and `allow_method_names_outside_object`, which are passed to the Rails field helpers.

::: tip Note
The endpoint receives the search text in `param`, such as `/fruits?q=gu`, and `?q=` when the listbox first opens. It
responds with the HTML of the matching options. The request sends `Accept: text/fragment+html`, and a response that
isn't 2xx shows the [error](#custom-error).

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::Autocomplete::OptionComponent.new(value: "guava", text: "Guava")) %>
<%= render(Impulse::Autocomplete::OptionComponent.new(value: "kiwi", text: "Kiwi")) %>
```

The `Impulse::Autocomplete::OptionComponent` also takes an optional `description` argument.

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::Autocomplete::OptionComponent.new(value: "kiwi", text: "Kiwi", description: "This is a fruit.")) %>
```

:::

## Examples

### Selecting an option

Pass an object that responds to the `value_method` and the `text_method`.

```erb{8}
<%= render(
  Impulse::AjaxSelectComponent.new(
    :post,
    :person_id,
    :id,
    :name,
    src: "/persons",
    selected: Person.find(1)
  )
) %>
```

::: tip
In case of multiple select, pass an array of objects to the `selected` argument.
:::

### Custom blankslate

A blankslate is displayed when the input's text does not match any of the options that are returned from the server.

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::AjaxSelectComponent.new(:post, :person_id, :id, :name, src: "/persons")) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_blankslate { "We couldn't find what you're looking for!" } %>
<% end %>
```

### Custom error

An error is displayed when the network request fails.

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::AjaxSelectComponent.new(:post, :person_id, :id, :name, src: "/persons")) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_error { "An error occurred. Please try again!" } %>
<% end %>
```

### Integrating with `form_with`

Wrap your `ajax_select` tag with the `impulse_form_with` method. The `f.ajax_select` tag accepts the same
[arguments](#arguments). Unlike `f.select`, it doesn't read the selection from the object, so pass `selected`.

```erb
<%= impulse_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.ajax_select :fruit_id, :id, :name, selected: f.object.fruit, src: "/fruits" %>
<% end %>
```

## Slots

### `with_blankslate`

Overwrite the default blankslate message by passing a block. It takes no arguments.

### `with_error`

Overwrite the default error message by passing a block. It takes no arguments.

## Imports

::: code-group

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';
```

```scss
@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';
```

:::

The styles need Bootstrap's Sass and the base styles loaded first. See [Import the styles](/introduction/getting-started#import-the-styles).

## JS API

[Read here](../js-api/autocomplete.md).

# Anchor

`Impulse::AnchorComponent` renders an `<awc-anchor>` element: a **floating element**, such as a tooltip or a menu,
that positions itself next to an **anchor** (another element on the page) and stays inside the viewport as the page
scrolls or resizes. It is configured entirely with attributes, so it needs no JavaScript of your own.

The anchor is often the **trigger** (the element that is clicked or hovered to show the floating element), but it
doesn't have to be. For example, a menu opened by a chevron button can be anchored to the whole field.

::: tip Anchor or `useFloatingUI`?
Use `Impulse::AnchorComponent` when you are writing markup and want something positioned. If you are writing your own
[`impulse`](https://github.com/Ambiki/impulse) element that opens and closes a floating element, use the
[`useFloatingUI`](../hooks/use-floating-ui.md) hook instead. Both share the same positioning logic and defaults.
:::

## Usage

```erb
<button type="button" id="anchor-button" class="btn btn-primary">Anchor</button>

<%= render(Impulse::AnchorComponent.new(anchor_id: "anchor-button", active: true, class: "popover bs-popover-auto")) do %>
  <div class="popover-body">I am anchored to the button!</div>
<% end %>
```

## Arguments

### Keyword arguments

| Name                | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| anchor\_id           | N/A       | The `id` of the element to position against.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| active              | `false`   | Whether the element is positioned when the page loads. Call [`start` and `stop`](../js-api/anchor.md) to change it from JavaScript. While `false`, the element stays where it was last placed, which before it first starts is the viewport's top-left corner. |
| placement           | `"bottom"`  | The preferred placement. The actual placement may vary to keep the element inside the viewport. One of `"top"`, `"top-start"`, `"top-end"`, `"right"`, `"right-start"`, `"right-end"`, `"bottom"`, `"bottom-start"`, `"bottom-end"`, `"left"`, `"left-start"`, or `"left-end"`.        |
| strategy            | `"fixed"`   | The value of the `position` CSS property. One of `"absolute"` or `"fixed"`.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| distance            | `0`       | The distance in pixels away from the anchor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| skidding            | `0`       | The distance in pixels along the anchor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| sync                | `nil`     | Matches the element's size to the anchor's. One of `"height"`, `"width"`, or `"both"`.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| flip                | `true`    | Flips the element to another placement when the preferred one doesn't fit.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| flip\_padding        | `0`       | The padding in pixels to keep from the viewport edge before flipping. Raised past `auto_size_padding` on the auto sized axis while `auto_size` is set.                                                                                                         |
| fallback\_placements | `[]`      | The placements to try, in order, when the preferred one doesn't fit. By default, the opposite side is tried.                                                                                                                                                   |
| fallback\_strategy   | `"bestFit"` | What to do when no placement fits. `"bestFit"` uses the placement that fits best, and `"initialPlacement"` uses `placement`, or the side `keep_flipped` keeps.                                                                                                     |
| keep\_flipped        | `false`   | Keeps the side the element flipped to until it's deactivated, instead of trying `placement` first on every reposition, so it doesn't jump back once its content shrinks. It still flips again when that side stops fitting.                                    |
| shift               | `true`    | Shifts the element along the anchor to keep it inside the viewport.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| shift\_padding       | `0`       | The padding in pixels to keep from the viewport edge while shifting.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| auto\_size           | `nil`     | Exposes the space available to the element as the `--awc-auto-size-height` and `--awc-auto-size-width` CSS custom properties. One of `"height"`, `"width"`, or `"both"`.                                                                                             |
| auto\_size\_padding   | `0`       | The padding in pixels to keep from the viewport edge when measuring the available space.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| arrow\_padding       | `0`       | The padding in pixels between the arrow and the edges of the element.                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Any other keyword arguments are passed to the `<awc-anchor>` element as HTML attributes.

## Examples

### Adding an arrow

Mark a child element with `data-arrow` to have it point at the anchor. The element's chosen placement is set as its
`x-placement` attribute, which you can use to style the arrow for each side.

```erb{2}
<%= render(Impulse::AnchorComponent.new(anchor_id: "anchor-button", active: true, distance: 8)) do %>
  <div class="arrow" data-arrow></div>
  <div class="popover-body">I am anchored to the button!</div>
<% end %>
```

### Fitting the viewport

Set `auto_size` and cap the element's size with the custom property it exposes, so a tall menu scrolls instead of
overflowing the viewport. When the cap squashes the element and the other side of the anchor has more room, the element
flips there.

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::AnchorComponent.new(anchor_id: "anchor-button", active: true, auto_size: "height", auto_size_padding: 8, class: "menu")) do %>
  ...
<% end %>
```

```css
.menu {
  max-height: var(--awc-auto-size-height);
  overflow-y: auto;
}
```

## Imports

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/anchor';
```

The component has no styles of its own.

## JS API

[Read here](../js-api/anchor.md).

# Clipboard copy

A button that copies text to the clipboard: a value rendered by the server, or the text of another element on the
page. It emits an event once the text is copied, or when it couldn't be, and enters a short feedback state you can
style. It shows and announces nothing of its own: how the user is told, with a toast, an icon swap, or not at all, is
up to your app.

## Usage

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::ClipboardCopyComponent.new(value: "https://example.com/meetings/123", class: "btn btn-primary")) do %>
  Copy link
<% end %>
```

The component renders `<awc-clipboard-copy>`, which is the button itself. It is announced as a button, takes focus,
and is pressed with a click, Enter, or Space, like a native `<button>`. Its content is what the button shows: a label,
an icon, or the value itself.

## Arguments

### Keyword arguments

| Name     | Default | Description                                                                                                       |
| ------   | ------- | -------------                                                                                                     |
| value    | `nil`   | The text to copy. When it isn't empty, it is copied instead of the copy source's text.                            |
| for      | `nil`   | The `id` of the copy source, the element whose text is copied when there is no `value`.                           |
| disabled | `false` | Whether the button ignores presses. A disabled button takes no focus and is announced as disabled.                |
| feedback\_duration | `2000` | How long, in milliseconds, the button stays in its feedback state after a press. See [Styling the feedback state](#styling-the-feedback-state). |

Any other keyword arguments, such as `class` or `aria`, are passed to the `<awc-clipboard-copy>` element as HTML
attributes. The component adds no classes of its own.

## Examples

### Copying another element's text

Name the copy source by its `id` with `for`. A form control (`<input>`, `<textarea>` or `<select>`) gives its value;
any other element gives its text as rendered, without its hidden content and with a line break between blocks. The
text is read when the button is pressed, so changes made after rendering are copied.

```erb
<pre id="setup-command">bundle exec rails db:setup</pre>

<%= render(Impulse::ClipboardCopyComponent.new(for: "setup-command", class: "btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary")) do %>
  Copy command
<% end %>
```

To copy something other than what the page shows, such as the text with a prefix, render it as the `value`.

### Icon-only button

A button that shows only an icon needs an accessible name, given with `aria-label`.

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::ClipboardCopyComponent.new(value: reference_number, class: "btn btn-sm", aria: { label: "Copy reference number" })) do %>
  <i class="bi bi-clipboard" aria-hidden="true"></i>
<% end %>
```

When the button has a visible label, leave out `aria-label`, or start it with the visible label, so that speech input
users can say what they see.

### Styling the feedback state

For a short while after a press, the button is in a feedback state: `:state(copied)` once the text is copied, or
`:state(error)` when nothing was. Style it to swap the icon, with no JavaScript. The state lasts 2 seconds; change it
with `feedback_duration:`, in milliseconds. Another press starts it over.

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::ClipboardCopyComponent.new(value: meeting_link, feedback_duration: 1000, class: "btn btn-sm copy-link", aria: { label: "Copy link" })) do %>
  <i class="bi bi-clipboard" aria-hidden="true"></i>
  <i class="bi bi-check2" aria-hidden="true"></i>
<% end %>
```

```css
.copy-link .bi-check2,
.copy-link:state(copied) .bi-clipboard {
  display: none;
}

.copy-link:state(copied) .bi-check2 {
  display: inline;
}
```

The state is a [custom state](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:state), not an attribute, so a DOM
morph doesn't end it early. Browsers without `:state()` (before Chrome 125, Firefox 126 and Safari 17.4) still copy,
without the feedback state.

### Announcing a copy

An icon swap is only seen. Screen reader users need to hear whether it copied too
([WCAG 4.1.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)), and the button doesn't announce it.
Listen for `awc-clipboard-copy:copied` and `awc-clipboard-copy:error`, which bubble, and put a message in a live
region, such as an element with `role="status"`. A toast that is one already does this.

```html
<div id="copy-status" role="status" class="sr-only"></div>
```

```js
// Emptied first, so that copying twice announces twice.
function announce(message) {
  const status = document.getElementById('copy-status');
  status.textContent = '';
  setTimeout(() => {
    status.textContent = message;
  }, 100);
}

document.addEventListener('awc-clipboard-copy:copied', () => announce('Copied to clipboard'));
document.addEventListener('awc-clipboard-copy:error', () => announce('Copying to the clipboard failed'));
```

The clipboard is only available on pages served over HTTPS or from `localhost`. Elsewhere, every press emits
`awc-clipboard-copy:error`. See the [JS API](../js-api/clipboard-copy.md) for each event's detail.

### Disabling the button

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::ClipboardCopyComponent.new(value: "Hello", disabled: true, class: "btn btn-primary")) do %>
  Copy
<% end %>
```

Like a native disabled button, it takes no focus, and listeners on it and its ancestors don't hear its clicks.
Bootstrap's `.btn:disabled` styles only match native form controls. Style a disabled button with
`awc-clipboard-copy[disabled]`, or add Bootstrap's `disabled` class.

## Imports

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/clipboard-copy';
```

The component has no styles of its own.

## JS API

[Read here](../js-api/clipboard-copy.md).

# Dialog

Dialog uses the native HTML `<dialog>` element under the hood which provides full accessibility out of the box and
solves z-index issues by rendering the element in the [top layer](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Top_layer).

## Usage

```erb
<button type="button">Open dialog</button>

<%= render(Impulse::DialogComponent.new(title: "My dialog")) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_body { "Dialog body" } %>
<% end %>
```

```js
const button = document.querySelector('button');
const dialog = document.querySelector('awc-dialog');
button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  dialog.requestShow();
});
```

## Arguments

### Keyword arguments

| Name                  | Default                  | Description                                                                                                                    |
| ------                | ---------                | -------------                                                                                                                  |
| title                 | N/A                      | The title of the dialog element.                                                                                               |
| id                    | `self.class.generate_id` | The `id` of the dialog element.                                                                                                |
| size                  | `:md`                    | The `size` of the dialog element. One of `:sm`, `:md`, or `:lg`.                                                               |
| center                | `true`                   | Whether or not to center the dialog vertically.                                                                                |
| fullscreen            | `:never`                 | Whether or not to render the dialog fullscreen. One of `:never`, `:always`, `:sm_down`, `:md_down`, `:lg_down`, or `:xl_down`. |
| hide\_on\_outside\_click | `true`                   | Whether or not to hide the dialog element when clicked outside.                                                                |

Any other keyword arguments are passed to the `<awc-dialog>` element as HTML attributes.

## Examples

### Body

You can add any arbitrary rich content inside the body by calling the `with_body` slot.

```erb{2}
<%= render(Impulse::DialogComponent.new(title: "My dialog")) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_body do %>
    <p>Dialog body</p>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

### Footer

You can add a footer by calling the `with_footer` slot.

```erb{2}
<%= render(Impulse::DialogComponent.new(title: "My dialog")) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_footer do %>
    <button type="button">Submit</button>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

### Adding a form

When the block renders content of its own, such as a form, the dialog renders that content instead of the `with_body`
and `with_footer` slots. Render the slots inside it with `<%= %>`, and give the element that wraps them the
`awc-dialog--scrollable` class, so that only the body scrolls.

```erb{2-11}
<%= render(Impulse::DialogComponent.new(title: "Edit profile")) do |c| %>
  <%= form_with url: "#", class: "awc-dialog--scrollable" do |f| %>
    <%= c.with_body do %>
      <%= f.label :name %>
      <%= f.text_field :name %>
    <% end %>
    <%= c.with_footer do %>
      <button type="reset" data-action="click->awc-dialog#requestHide">Cancel</button>
      <%= f.submit %>
    <% end %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

If your arbitrary content comes from a partial as is the case with many `form_with` partials, you can use the
`Impulse::Dialog::BodyComponent` and `Impulse::Dialog::FooterComponent` to render the body and footer of the dialog
component respectively.

```erb{2}
<%= render(Impulse::DialogComponent.new(title: "Edit profile")) do %>
  <%= render "shared/form" %>
<% end %>
```

```erb{4,8}
<%# app/views/shared/_form.html.erb %>

<%= form_with url: "#", class: "awc-dialog--scrollable" do |f| %>
  <%= render(Impulse::Dialog::BodyComponent.new) do %>
    <%= f.label :name %>
    <%= f.text_field :name %>
  <% end %>
  <%= render(Impulse::Dialog::FooterComponent.new) do %>
    <button type="reset" data-action="click->awc-dialog#requestHide">Cancel</button>
    <%= f.submit %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

### Closing the dialog

Add the `data-action="click->awc-dialog#requestHide"` attribute on the `button` element to close the dialog when clicking it.

`requestHide` emits the cancelable `awc-dialog:hide` event first, so a listener can keep the dialog open, for example
while a form inside it has unsaved changes. `hide` closes it without asking.

```erb{3}
<%= render(Impulse::DialogComponent.new(title: "Edit your profile")) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_body do %>
    <button type="button" data-action="click->awc-dialog#requestHide">Close</button>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

### Nested dialogs

You can nest as many dialogs as you want and it will be stacked on top of the parent dialog.

```erb{7-9}
<button type="button">Open dialog</button>

<%= render(Impulse::DialogComponent.new(title: "Edit your profile")) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_body do %>
    <p>Body contents...</p>
    <button type="button">Open nested dialog</button>
    <%= render(Impulse::DialogComponent.new(title: "Nested dialog", size: :sm)) do |nested| %>
      <% nested.with_body { "This is a nested dialog." } %>
    <% end %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

## Slots

### `with_body`

The body of the dialog.

| Name          | Default   | Description                                                               |
| ------        | --------- | -------------                                                             |
| `system_args` | `{}`      | HTML attributes for the slot's element.                                   |

### `with_footer`

The footer of the dialog.

| Name          | Default   | Description                                                               |
| ------        | --------- | -------------                                                             |
| `system_args` | `{}`      | HTML attributes for the slot's element.                                   |

## Imports

::: code-group

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/dialog';
```

```scss
@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/dialog';
```

:::

The styles need Bootstrap's Sass and the base styles loaded first. See [Import the styles](/introduction/getting-started#import-the-styles).

## JS API

[Read here](../js-api/dialog.md).

url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/components/popover.md

# Popover

A popover is a floating panel that can display rich content like navigation menus and mobile menus.

## Usage

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::PopoverComponent.new) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_trigger(class: "btn btn-primary") { "Toggle popover" } %>
  <% c.with_body do %>
    <span>And here's some amazing content. It's very engaging. Right?</span>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

## Arguments

### Keyword arguments

| Name      | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------    | --------- | -------------                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| title     | `nil`     | The title of the popover.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| placement | `"bottom"`  | The preferred placement of the popover. The actual placement may vary to keep the element inside the viewport. One of `"top"`, `"top-start"`, `"top-end"`, `"right"`, `"right-start"`, `"right-end"`, `"bottom"`, `"bottom-start"`, `"bottom-end"`, `"left"`, `"left-start"`, or `"left-end"`. |
| strategy  | `"fixed"`   | The value of the `position` CSS property. One of `"absolute"` or `"fixed"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Any other keyword arguments are passed to the `<awc-popover>` element as HTML attributes, such as `open: true` to render
it open.

## Examples

### Adding a title

You can add a title by setting the `title` argument on the component. It will also add a close button next to it.

```erb{1}
<%= render(Impulse::PopoverComponent.new(title: "Activity feed")) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_trigger { "Open feed" } %>
  <% c.with_body { "Body" } %>
<% end %>
```

### Custom header

You can customize the header to add rich content instead of a simple title by calling the `with_header` slot.

```erb{3-6}
<%= render(Impulse::PopoverComponent.new) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_trigger { "Toggle popover" } %>
  <% c.with_header do %>
    <h2>Custom title</h2>
    <button type="button">Action button</button>
  <% end %>
  <% c.with_body do %>
    <span>And here's some amazing content. It's very engaging. Right?</span>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

::: tip Note
You are encouraged to use the `title` argument if there aren't any rich content inside the header.
:::

### Closing the popover

Add the `data-action="click->awc-popover#requestHide"` attribute on the `button` element to close the popover when clicking it.

`requestHide` emits the cancelable `awc-popover:hide` event first, so a listener can keep the popover open, for example
while a form inside it has unsaved changes. `hide` closes it without asking.

```erb{4}
<%= render(Impulse::PopoverComponent.new(title: "Activity feed")) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_trigger { "Toggle popover" } %>
  <% c.with_body do %>
    <button type="button" data-action="click->awc-popover#requestHide">Close</button>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

### Nesting popovers

You can nest as many popovers as you want and it will be stacked on top of the parent popover. A nested popover counts
as part of its parent, so moving focus or clicking into it doesn't close the parent. A click outside both, or focus
moving out of both, closes them together, the nested popover first. Escape closes the popover focus is in.

```erb{4-7}
<%= render(Impulse::PopoverComponent.new) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_trigger { "Open" } %>
  <% c.with_body do %>
    <%= render(Impulse::PopoverComponent.new) do |nested| %>
      <% nested.with_trigger { "Open nested popover" } %>
      <% nested.with_body { "Nested contents" } %>
    <% end %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

## Accessibility

The popover is a non-modal dialog, rendered in the browser's [top
layer](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Top_layer) so that no `z-index` or `overflow` can hide it.

* The popover has `role="dialog"`, labelled by the `title`, or by the trigger when there is no title or a custom header
  replaces it. The trigger has `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
* Opening it moves focus into the popover: to the element with `autofocus`, else the first element you can Tab to,
  else the popover itself. A popover rendered open doesn't take focus.
* Escape, a click outside, and focus moving out of the popover, such as Tab past its last element, all ask it to close.
* Closing it returns focus to the trigger when focus was inside the popover, or lost. When focus has moved on to
  something else, such as a field clicked outside, it stays there.
* Closing it closes the popovers nested in it first. A user action asks them first, and one that refuses keeps the
  popover open.

## Slots

### `with_trigger`

The trigger, a `<button>` that shows or hides the popover. Required: the popover renders nothing without it.

| Name          | Default   | Description                                                               |
| ------        | --------- | -------------                                                             |
| `system_args` | `{}`      | HTML attributes for the slot's element.                                   |

### `with_header`

The header of the popover. If you just want to change the title of the popover, pass the `title` argument to
the component.

| Name          | Default   | Description                                                               |
| ------        | --------- | -------------                                                             |
| `system_args` | `{}`      | HTML attributes for the slot's element.                                   |

### `with_body`

The body of the popover.

| Name          | Default   | Description                                                               |
| ------        | --------- | -------------                                                             |
| `tag`         | `:div`    | The name of the HTML tag.                                                 |
| `system_args` | `{}`      | HTML attributes for the slot's element.                                   |

## Imports

::: code-group

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/popover';
```

```scss
@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/popover';
```

:::

The styles need Bootstrap's Sass and the base styles loaded first. See [Import the styles](/introduction/getting-started#import-the-styles).

## JS API

[Read here](../js-api/popover.md).

url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/components/select.md
---
# Select

Select allows a user to filter through a list of pre-defined sets of options and select one or multiple values.

## Usage

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::SelectComponent.new(:post, :person_id, Person.all.collect { |p| [p.name, p.id] })) %>
```

## Arguments

### Positional arguments

| Name        | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------      | --------- | -------------                                                                                                                                                                    |
| object\_name | N/A       | The name of the object.                                                                                                                                                          |
| method\_name | N/A       | The name of the method.                                                                                                                                                          |
| choices     | `[]`      | An array of choices, similar to what you would pass to the native Rails [`select`](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/FormOptionsHelper.html#method-i-select) tag. |

### Keyword arguments

| Name              | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                       |
| ------            | --------- | -------------                                                                                                                                     |
| selected          | `nil`     | The `value` of the option that you want to force select.                                                                                          |
| size              | `:md`     | The size of the select control. One of `:sm`, `:md`, or `:lg`.                                                                                    |
| name              | `nil`     | The name of the field. By default, Rails automatically creates a `name` string based on the `object_name` and `method_name`.                      |
| input\_id          | `nil`     | The id of the input field.                                                                                                                        |
| placeholder       | `nil`     | The placeholder text that is displayed within the input field.                                                                                    |
| include\_hidden    | `true`    | Only applies to a `multiple` select. See the "Gotcha" section of the Rails [`select`](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/FormOptionsHelper.html#method-i-select) tag. |
| disabled          | `false`   | Disables the select control.                                                                                                                      |
| required          | `false`   | Makes the select control a required field.                                                                                                        |
| multiple          | `false`   | Whether multiple values can be selected or not.                                                                                                   |
| clearable         | `true`    | Whether the clear button should be shown or not.                                                                                                  |
| auto\_size         | `true`    | If `true`, caps the listbox's height to the space between it and the edge of the viewport, so a long list scrolls instead of running off screen.  |
| auto\_size\_padding | `4`       | The space in pixels to keep between the listbox and the edge of the viewport when `auto_size` is enabled.                                         |

Any other keyword arguments are passed to the `<awc-autocomplete>` element as HTML attributes, except `namespace`,
`skip_default_ids` and `allow_method_names_outside_object`, which are passed to the Rails field helpers.

## Examples

### Rendering custom options

Instead of passing an array of choices to the component, you can also render the options as a block. This provides
more flexibility, and you can pass any HTML attributes to each option.

```erb{2-4}
<%= render(Impulse::SelectComponent.new(:post, :person_id)) do |c| %>
  <% Person.all.each do |person| %>
    <% c.with_option(value: person.id, text: person.display_name, disabled: person.on_vacation?) %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

### Selecting an option

You can pass the `value` of the option to the `selected` argument and it will be selected by default.

```erb{6}
<%= render(
  Impulse::SelectComponent.new(
    :user,
    :fruit_id,
    ["Apple", "Mango"],
    selected: "Mango"
  )
) %>
```

::: tip
In case of multiple select, pass an array of values to the `selected` argument, e.g. `["Apple", "Mango"]`.
:::

### Add inline attributes to options

You can optionally provide HTML attributes as the last element of the array.

```erb{5}
<%= render(
  Impulse::SelectComponent.new(
    :user,
    :country_id,
    ["Denmark", ["USA", { class: "bold", disabled: true }], "Sweden"]
  )
) %>
```

::: warning
Do not add "aria-selected" attribute to an option. If you want to select an option, pass the option's value to the
[`selected`](#selecting-an-option) argument.
:::

### Add description to an option

You can optionally add an inline description or pass the description attribute to the option slot.

```erb{6,16}
<%# Inline %>
<%= render(
  Impulse::SelectComponent.new(
    :user,
    :country_id,
    [["USA", { description: "USA is a country." }]]
  )
) %>

<%# Block %>
<%= render(Impulse::SelectComponent.new(:user, :country_id)) do |c| %>
  <% Country.all.each do |country| %>
    <% c.with_option(
      value: country.id,
      text: country.display_name,
      description: country.description
    ) %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

### Grouping options

Like Rails' [`grouped_options_for_select`](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/FormOptionsHelper.html#method-i-grouped_options_for_select),
the select component also supports grouping options. You can pass an array or a hash of grouped options.

```erb
<%
  grouped_options = [
    ["North America", [["United States", "US"], ["Canada", "CA", {disabled: true}]]],
    ["Europe", ["Denmark", "Germany"]]
  ]
%>

<%= render(Impulse::SelectComponent.new(:user, :country_id, grouped_options, selected: "US")) %>
```

```erb
<%
  grouped_options = {
    "North America" => [["United States", "US"], "Canada"],
    "Europe" => ["Denmark", "Germany"]
  }
%>

<%= render(Impulse::SelectComponent.new(:user, :country_id, grouped_options, selected: "US")) %>
```

When rendering the options as a block, wrap them in `with_group`.

```erb{3,5}
<%= render(Impulse::SelectComponent.new(:user, :country_id, selected: "US")) do |c| %>
  <% Continent.all.each do |continent| %>
    <% c.with_group(title: continent.name) do |group| %>
      <% continent.countries.each do |country| %>
        <% group.with_option(value: country.code, text: country.name) %>
      <% end %>
    <% end %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

### Custom blankslate

A blankslate is displayed when the input's text does not match any of the options.

```erb{2}
<%= render(Impulse::SelectComponent.new(:post, :person_id, Person.all.collect { |p| [p.name, p.id] })) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_blankslate { "We could not find that person in our directory!" } %>
<% end %>
```

### Integrating with `form_with`

Wrap your `select` tag with the `impulse_form_with` method. The `f.select` tag accepts the same
[arguments](#arguments), and selects the attribute's value unless you pass `selected`.

```erb
<%= impulse_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.select :person_id, Person.all.collect { |p| [p.name, p.id] } %>
<% end %>
```

## Slots

### `with_option`

Customize the options by rendering a collection of the `with_option` block.

| Name          | Default   | Description                                                               |
| ------        | --------- | -------------                                                             |
| `value`       | N/A       | The value of the option.                                                  |
| `text`        | N/A       | The text of the option.                                                   |
| `description` | `nil`     | An optional secondary description displayed below the option's text.      |
| `system_args` | `{}`      | HTML attributes for the slot's element.                                   |

### `with_group`

Groups options under a title. Add the options with the group's `with_option`, which takes the same arguments as
`with_option` above. A group with no options isn't rendered.

| Name          | Default   | Description                                                               |
| ------        | --------- | -------------                                                             |
| `title`       | N/A       | The title displayed above the group's options.                            |
| `system_args` | `{}`      | HTML attributes for the slot's element.                                   |

### `with_blankslate`

Overwrite the default blankslate message by passing a block. It takes no arguments.

## Imports

::: code-group

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';
```

```scss
@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';
```

:::

The styles need Bootstrap's Sass and the base styles loaded first. See [Import the styles](/introduction/getting-started#import-the-styles).

## JS API

[Read here](../js-api/autocomplete.md).

# Spinner

Indicate the loading state of a component or a page.

## Usage

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::SpinnerComponent.new) %>
```

## Arguments

### Keyword arguments

| Name    | Default     | Description                                                                                                          |
| ------  | ---------   | -------------                                                                                                        |
| variant | `:secondary` | The color of the spinner. One of `:primary`, `:secondary`, `:success`, `:danger`, `:warning`, `:info`, `:light`, or `:dark`. |
| label   | `"Loading"`  | The accessible text that describes the current state of the component or a page.                                              |

Any other keyword arguments are passed to the spinner's `<div>` element as HTML attributes.

## Examples

### Changing the color

Set one of the accepted variants as the `variant` argument.

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::SpinnerComponent.new(variant: :primary)) %>
<%= render(Impulse::SpinnerComponent.new(variant: :danger)) %>
<%= render(Impulse::SpinnerComponent.new(variant: :info)) %>
```

# Time zone select

Time zone select allows a user to filter through a list of default time zones and select one or multiple values.

## Usage

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::TimeZoneSelectComponent.new(:user, :time_zone)) %>
```

## Arguments

### Positional arguments

| Name           | Default   | Description                                                                  |
| ------         | --------- | -------------                                                                |
| object\_name    | N/A       | The name of the object.                                                      |
| method\_name    | N/A       | The name of the method.                                                      |
| priority\_zones | `nil`     | The time zones listed above the rest: an array of zones, or a `Regexp` that each zone is matched against. |

### Keyword arguments

| Name                 | Default                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------               | ---------                 | -------------                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| selected             | `nil`                     | The `value` of the option that you want to force select.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| default              | `nil`                     | The `value` of the option that you want to select if the `selected` is `nil`.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| model                | `ActiveSupport::TimeZone` | Where the zones come from: an object whose `all` returns them. Each zone must respond to `name` (the option's value) and `to_s` (its text), and to `match?` when `priority_zones` is a `Regexp`. |
| priority\_zones\_title | `"Prioritized time zones"` | The title of the group of time zones that have been prioritized.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| size                 | `:md`                     | The size of the select control. One of `:sm`, `:md`, or `:lg`.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| name                 | `nil`                     | The name of the field. By default, Rails automatically creates a `name` string based on the `object_name` and `method_name`.                                                                                                                     |
| input\_id             | `nil`                     | The id of the input field.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| placeholder          | `nil`                     | The placeholder text that is displayed within the input field.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| include\_hidden       | `true`                    | Only applies to a `multiple` select. See the "Gotcha" section of the Rails [`select`](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/FormOptionsHelper.html#method-i-select) tag.                                                                                             |
| disabled             | `false`                   | Disables the select control.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| required             | `false`                   | Makes the select control a required field.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| multiple             | `false`                   | Whether multiple values can be selected or not.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| clearable            | `true`                    | Whether the clear button should be shown or not.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| auto\_size            | `true`                    | If `true`, caps the listbox's height to the space between it and the edge of the viewport, so a long list scrolls instead of running off screen.                                                                                                 |
| auto\_size\_padding    | `4`                       | The space in pixels to keep between the listbox and the edge of the viewport when `auto_size` is enabled.                                                                                                                                        |

Any other keyword arguments are passed to the `<awc-autocomplete>` element as HTML attributes, except `namespace`,
`skip_default_ids` and `allow_method_names_outside_object`, which are passed to the Rails field helpers.

## Examples

### Prioritizing zones

Pass an array of [`ActiveSupport::TimeZone`](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveSupport/TimeZone.html),
[`ActiveSupport::TimeZone.us_zones`](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveSupport/TimeZone.html#method-c-us_zones)
for a list of US time zones, [`ActiveSupport::TimeZone.country_zones(country_code)`](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveSupport/TimeZone.html#method-c-country_zones)
for another country’s time zones, or a [`Regexp`](https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master/Regexp.html) to select the zones
of your choice. The rest are listed after them, under "Other".

```erb
<%= render(Impulse::TimeZoneSelectComponent.new(:user, :time_zone, ActiveSupport::TimeZone.us_zones)) %>
<%= render(Impulse::TimeZoneSelectComponent.new(:user, :time_zone, [ActiveSupport::TimeZone["Alaska"], ActiveSupport::TimeZone["Hawaii"]])) %>
<%= render(Impulse::TimeZoneSelectComponent.new(:user, :time_zone, /Australia/)) %>
```

### Custom blankslate

A blankslate is displayed when the input's text does not match any of the options.

```erb{2}
<%= render(Impulse::TimeZoneSelectComponent.new(:user, :time_zone)) do |c| %>
  <% c.with_blankslate { "We could not find that time zone in our directory!" } %>
<% end %>
```

### Integrating with `form_with`

Wrap your `time_zone_select` tag with the `impulse_form_with` method. The `f.time_zone_select` tag accepts the same
[arguments](#arguments), and selects the attribute's value unless you pass `selected`. `default` applies when the
attribute is `nil`.

```erb
<%= impulse_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.time_zone_select :time_zone %>
<% end %>

<%= impulse_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.time_zone_select :time_zone, ActiveSupport::TimeZone.us_zones %>
<% end %>

<%= impulse_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.time_zone_select :time_zone, nil, default: "Hawaii" %>
<% end %>

<%= impulse_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.time_zone_select :time_zone do |c| %>
    <% c.with_blankslate { "Time zone not found!" } %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

## Slots

### `with_blankslate`

Overwrite the default blankslate message by passing a block. It takes no arguments.

## Imports

::: code-group

```js
import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';
```

```scss
@import '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';
```

:::

The styles need Bootstrap's Sass and the base styles loaded first. See [Import the styles](/introduction/getting-started#import-the-styles).

## JS API

# Anchor API

```js
const anchor = document.querySelector('awc-anchor');
```

## Properties

### `anchorId`

The `id` of the element to position against. Changing it while the element is active moves the element to the new
anchor.

```js
anchor.anchorId = 'other-button';
```

### `active`

Whether the element is kept next to its anchor. Setting it starts or stops the element, as `start` and `stop` do.

```js
anchor.active;
// => true
```

### Positioning options

Every other argument of the [Anchor component](../components/anchor.md#keyword-arguments) is also a property, in
camelCase, such as `placement`, `flipPadding` or `autoSize`.

```js
anchor.placement = 'top';
```

## Methods

### `start`

Positions the element and keeps it next to its anchor as the page scrolls or resizes, until `stop` is called. An
element rendered with `active: true` starts on its own.

```js
// <awc-anchor> only positions the element; showing it is up to you.
anchor.hidden = false;
anchor.start();
```

### `stop`

Stops keeping the element next to its anchor. It stays where it was last placed. Resolves once it has stopped, on the
next frame if it was running, so you can wait for it before hiding the element.

```js
await anchor.stop();
anchor.hidden = true; // or however your app hides it
```

### `reposition`

Positions the element straight away. Changing an option such as `placement` otherwise takes effect from the next time
the element is repositioned, e.g. when the page scrolls. Does nothing while the element is stopped.

```js
anchor.placement = 'top';
await anchor.reposition();
```

## Events

`<awc-anchor>` doesn't emit any events.

---

---
url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/js-api/autocomplete.md
---
# Autocomplete API

```js
const autocomplete = document.querySelector('awc-autocomplete');
```

## TypeScript

The selection mode (single vs. multiple) determines the type of `value` and the arguments
`removeValue` accepts, and the source (local vs. ajax) determines whether `setValue` requires
the `text` argument. TypeScript resolves these automatically when you narrow on the `multiple` and
`ajax` properties:

```ts
const autocomplete = document.querySelector('awc-autocomplete')!;

if (autocomplete.multiple) {
  autocomplete.value; // string[]
  autocomplete.removeValue('1'); // value argument is required
} else {
  autocomplete.value; // string
  autocomplete.removeValue(); // no argument
}

if (autocomplete.ajax) {
  autocomplete.setValue('1', 'One'); // text is required
} else {
  autocomplete.setValue('1'); // text is optional
}
```

If you already know the mode at the call site, pass the exported type to `querySelector` instead
of narrowing:

```ts
import type {
  MultipleAutocompleteElement,
  SingleAutocompleteElement,
} from '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';

const multi = document.querySelector<MultipleAutocompleteElement>('awc-autocomplete')!;
multi.value; // string[]

const single = document.querySelector<SingleAutocompleteElement>('awc-autocomplete')!;
single.value; // string
```

If you already know the source at the call site, you can also pass the exported type to
`querySelector` instead of narrowing on `ajax`:

```ts
import type {
  AjaxAutocompleteElement,
  LocalAutocompleteElement,
} from '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete';

const ajax = document.querySelector<AjaxAutocompleteElement>('awc-autocomplete')!;
ajax.setValue('1', 'One'); // text is required
ajax.setValue('1'); // ✗ type error

const local = document.querySelector<LocalAutocompleteElement>('awc-autocomplete')!;
local.setValue('1'); // text is optional
```

Each alias leaves the other dimension open, but they are composable — pass the other dimension as a
type argument to pin both at once:

```ts
const el = document.querySelector<MultipleAutocompleteElement<'ajax'>>('awc-autocomplete')!;
el.value; // string[]
el.setValue('1', 'One'); // text is required

// `AjaxAutocompleteElement<'multiple'>` resolves to the same type.
```

## Properties

### `open`

Whether the listbox is open. Setting it, or adding or removing the `open` attribute, shows or hides the listbox as
`show` and `hide` do. A removed autocomplete keeps `open`, and opens its listbox again when it's added back.

```js
autocomplete.open;
// => false
autocomplete.open = true;
```

### `value`

The selected value(s). For a single select this is a `string`; for a multiple select it is a `string[]`.

```js
// Multiple select
autocomplete.value;
// => ['1', '2']

// Single select
autocomplete.value;
// => '1'
```

### `multiple`

Whether multiple values can be selected. Narrowing on this resolves mode-dependent types — see
[TypeScript](#typescript).

```js
autocomplete.multiple;
// => true
```

### `ajax`

Whether the options are fetched from the server (i.e. the `src` attribute is set). Narrowing on this resolves
source-dependent types — see [TypeScript](#typescript).

```js
autocomplete.ajax;
// => true
```

### `activeOption`

The option that has the `data-active` attribute.

```js
autocomplete.activeOption;
```

### `visibleOptions`

All the visible options of the autocomplete element.

```js
autocomplete.visibleOptions;
```

### `options`

All the options of the autocomplete element.

```js
autocomplete.options;
```

### `form`

The parent form element.

```js
autocomplete.form;
```

## Methods

### `show`

Shows the listbox. Emits `awc-autocomplete:shown`, but not the cancelable `awc-autocomplete:show`.

```js
autocomplete.show();
```

### `hide`

Hides the listbox. Emits `awc-autocomplete:hidden`, but not the cancelable `awc-autocomplete:hide`.

```js
await autocomplete.hide();
```

### `requestShow`

Shows the listbox as if the user asked to. Emits a cancelable `awc-autocomplete:show`, and does nothing if it is
prevented.

```js
autocomplete.requestShow();
```

### `requestHide`

Hides the listbox as if the user asked to. Emits a cancelable `awc-autocomplete:hide`, and does nothing if it is
prevented.

```js
await autocomplete.requestHide();
```

### `setValue`

Sets the value of the element. When the options are fetched from the server, the `text` argument is required (the
option is not in the DOM, so its text cannot be derived); for local options it is optional. See
[TypeScript](#typescript) for how to enforce this at compile time.

```js
// Multiple select
autocomplete.setValue('apple', 'Apple');
autocomplete.value;
// => ['apple']

// When the options are not loaded from the server, you do not have to pass the text argument.
autocomplete.setValue('apple');
autocomplete.value;
// => ['apple']
```

### `removeValue`

Removes a value from the element.

```js
// Multiple select
autocomplete.removeValue('apple');
autocomplete.value;
// => []
```

::: tip
The `value` argument is required for a multiple select and is not used by a single select (which clears its value when
`removeValue()` is called). TypeScript enforces this when the mode is known — see [TypeScript](#typescript).
:::

### `activate`

Activates an option by setting the `data-active` attribute, and scrolls it into view. Pass `{ scroll: false }` to
skip the scrolling.

```js
const option = autocomplete.options[0];
autocomplete.activate(option, { scroll: false });
```

### `deactivate`

Deactivates the active option by removing the `data-active` attribute.

```js
autocomplete.deactivate();
```

### `clear`

Deselects all the selected options.

```js
autocomplete.clear();
```

### `reset`

Resets the autocomplete value to its initial state.

```js
autocomplete.reset();
```

### `focus`

Sets the focus on the input element. It also accepts the native focus
[options](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/focus#parameters) object.

```js
autocomplete.focus({ preventScroll: true });
```

### `blur`

Removes keyboard focus from the input element.

```js
autocomplete.blur();
```

### `reposition`

Positions the listbox straight away. Does nothing while the listbox is closed.

```js
await autocomplete.reposition();
```

## Events

Events work as they do on native elements. A user action (pressing the control or typing in the input, Escape,
Alt+ArrowDown, Alt+ArrowUp, an outside click, the input losing focus, committing an option in a single select,
clearing), or a `requestShow` or `requestHide` call, first emits a cancelable `show` or `hide`; calling
`preventDefault()` on it keeps the listbox closed or open. `show()`, `hide()` and changing `open` act directly and emit
no `show` or `hide`, and neither does closing because the form was reset. `shown` and `hidden` fire after every open
and close. Connecting, moving and removing the element emit nothing.

Like the other events, `show` and `hide` bubble. A listener on an element that contains other autocompletes receives
their `show` and `hide` too, so check `event.target` before preventing one.

Like `input` and `change`, `commit`, `clear`, `remove` and `reset` fire after the value has changed, and only when the
user changed it or the form reset: `setValue`, `removeValue`, `clear` and `reset` called from code emit nothing.

`commit` reports the option's state after the commit in `event.detail.selected`: `true` when the commit selected it,
`false` when it deselected it in a multiple select.

```js
autocomplete.addEventListener('awc-autocomplete:commit', (event) => {
  const { value, selected } = event.detail;
  console.log(selected ? `Selected ${value}` : `Deselected ${value}`);
});
```

::: warning
In a single select, committing the option that is already selected emits `commit` with `selected: true`, although the
value doesn't change. A future release will stop emitting it, as a native `<select>` emits no `change` when the user
selects the option that is already selected ([#310](https://github.com/Ambiki/impulse_view_components/issues/310)).
:::

| Name                      | Bubbles | Cancelable | Description                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `awc-autocomplete:show`   | `true`  | `true`     | Fires before the listbox opens for a user action or `requestShow`.                                                                                                                     |
| `awc-autocomplete:shown`  | `true`  | `false`    | Fires after the listbox has opened.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `awc-autocomplete:hide`   | `true`  | `true`     | Fires before the listbox closes for a user action or `requestHide`.                                                                                                                    |
| `awc-autocomplete:hidden` | `true`  | `false`    | Fires after the listbox has closed.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `awc-autocomplete:commit` | `true`  | `false`    | Fires when the user commits an option. `event.detail` carries the option as `target`, its `value`, its `text`, and `selected`: whether the option is selected after the commit. |
| `awc-autocomplete:clear`  | `true`  | `false`    | Fires when the user deselects all the options with the clear button.                                                                                                                  |
| `awc-autocomplete:remove` | `true`  | `false`    | Fires when the user removes a tag. `event.detail` carries the tag as `target`, its `value`, and its `text`.                                                                            |
| `awc-autocomplete:reset`  | `true`  | `false`    | Fires when the parent form has been reset.                                                                                                                                             |
| `loadstart`               | `false` | `false`    | Fires when the autocomplete starts the network request.                                                                                                                                |
| `load`                    | `false` | `false`    | Fires when the autocomplete fetches the options successfully from the server.                                                                                                          |
| `error`                   | `false` | `false`    | Fires when the autocomplete fails to fetch the options from the server.                                                                                                                |
| `loadend`                 | `false` | `false`    | Fires when the autocomplete finishes the network request.                                                                                                                              |

The `commit` and `remove` details are exported as `AwcAutocompleteCommitEvent` and `AwcAutocompleteRemoveEvent` from
`@ambiki/impulse-view-components/autocomplete`.

---

---
url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/js-api/clipboard-copy.md
---
# Clipboard copy API

```js
const clipboardCopy = document.querySelector('awc-clipboard-copy');
```

## Properties

### `value`

The text to copy. When empty, the copy source's text is copied instead.

```js
clipboardCopy.value = 'https://example.com/meetings/456';
```

### `for`

The `id` of the copy source. A form control gives its value, any other element its rendered text.

```js
clipboardCopy.for = 'setup-command';
```

### `disabled`

Whether the element ignores presses. Like a native disabled button, it takes no focus and its clicks don't reach
listeners.

```js
clipboardCopy.disabled = true;
```

### `feedbackDuration`

How long, in milliseconds, the feedback state lasts. Defaults to `2000`.

```js
clipboardCopy.feedbackDuration = 1000;
```

## Methods

### `copy`

Copies the text, even when disabled. Resolves once `copied` or `error` is emitted; never rejects.

Firefox and Safari only allow clipboard writes during a user gesture, so call it from one, such as a click handler.

```js
menuItem.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  await clipboardCopy.copy();
  menu.hide();
});
```

## States

After a copy, the element is in a [custom state](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:state) for
[`feedbackDuration`](#feedbackduration). Another copy restarts it.

| State    | Description                         |
| ------   | ------------                        |
| `copied` | The text was copied.                |
| `error`  | Nothing was copied.                 |

```js
clipboardCopy.matches(':state(copied)');
```

## Events

A press is a click, Enter, or Space. `preventDefault()` doesn't stop it; disable the element instead. If the press
removes the element, its events don't reach `document`.

| Name                        | Bubbles | Cancelable | Description                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------                      | ------- | ---------- | ------------                                                                                                                                                  |
| `awc-clipboard-copy:copied` | `true`  | `false`    | Fires once the text is copied. `event.detail.text` is the copied text.                                                                                        |
| `awc-clipboard-copy:error`  | `true`  | `false`    | Fires when nothing was copied. `event.detail.error` is a `NotFoundError` (nothing to copy), a `NotSupportedError` (no Clipboard API), or the browser's rejection. |

The details are exported as `AwcClipboardCopyCopiedEvent` and `AwcClipboardCopyErrorEvent` from
`@ambiki/impulse-view-components/clipboard-copy`.

```ts
document.addEventListener('awc-clipboard-copy:copied', (event) => {
  const { text } = event.detail;
});
```
