---
url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/js-api/dialog.md
---
# Dialog API

```js
const dialog = document.querySelector('awc-dialog');
```

## Properties

### `open`

Whether the dialog is open. Setting it, or adding or removing the `open` attribute, shows or hides the dialog as `show`
and `hide` do, so `<awc-dialog open>` opens modally, unlike a native `<dialog open>`. A removed dialog keeps `open`, and
opens again when it's added back.

```js
dialog.open;
// => false
dialog.open = true;
```

### `hideOnOutsideClick`

Whether a click outside the dialog asks it to close. Defaults to `true`.

```js
dialog.hideOnOutsideClick = false;
```

## Methods

### `show`

Shows the dialog. Emits `awc-dialog:shown`, but not the cancelable `awc-dialog:show`.

```js
dialog.show();
```

### `hide`

Hides the dialog, and any dialog nested in it first. Emits `awc-dialog:hidden`, but not the cancelable
`awc-dialog:hide`.

```js
await dialog.hide();
```

### `requestShow`

Shows the dialog as if the user asked to. Emits a cancelable `awc-dialog:show`, and does nothing if it is prevented.

```js
dialog.requestShow();
```

### `requestHide`

Hides the dialog as if the user asked to. Emits a cancelable `awc-dialog:hide`, and does nothing if it is prevented.

```js
await dialog.requestHide();
```

### `hideWithoutEmitting`

Hides the dialog, and any dialog nested in it, without emitting any `awc-dialog` events. Like `hide`, it removes
`open`.

```js
dialog.hideWithoutEmitting();
```

## Events

Events work as they do on native elements. A user action, or a `requestShow` or `requestHide` call, first emits a
cancelable `show` or `hide`; calling `preventDefault()` on it stops the dialog from opening or closing. `show()`,
`hide()` and changing `open` act directly, like a native `<dialog>`'s `close()`, and emit no `show` or `hide`. `shown`
and `hidden` fire after every open and close, whatever caused it. Connecting, moving and removing the element emit
nothing.

Like the other events, `show` and `hide` bubble. A listener on an element that contains other dialogs receives their
`show` and `hide` too, so check `event.target` before preventing one.

| Name                | Bubbles | Cancelable | Description                                                                                                   |
| ------              | ------- | ---------- | ------------                                                                                                  |
| `awc-dialog:show`   | `true`  | `true`     | Fires before the dialog opens for `requestShow`.                                                              |
| `awc-dialog:shown`  | `true`  | `false`    | Fires after the dialog has opened.                                                                            |
| `awc-dialog:hide`   | `true`  | `true`     | Fires before the dialog closes for a user action or `requestHide`: a close button, Escape, or an outside click. |
| `awc-dialog:hidden` | `true`  | `false`    | Fires after the dialog has closed, including when a `<form method="dialog">` closes it.                       |

::: tip
Browsers let a page keep a dialog open only on the first Escape after the user interacts with it. If the user presses
Escape again, the dialog closes without an `awc-dialog:hide`, and only `awc-dialog:hidden` fires.
:::

---

---
url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/js-api/popover.md
---
# Popover API

```js
const popover = document.querySelector('awc-popover');
```

## Properties

### `open`

Whether the popover is open. Setting it, or adding or removing the `open` attribute, shows or hides the popover as
`show` and `hide` do. A removed popover keeps `open`, and opens again when it's added back.

```js
popover.open;
// => false
popover.open = true;
```

### `placement` and `strategy`

The same options as on the [Popover component](../components/popover.md#keyword-arguments). Changing `placement`
repositions the popover straight away.

```js
popover.placement = 'top';
```

## Methods

### `show`

Shows the popover, hides any other open popover except the ones it is nested in, and moves focus into it. Emits
`awc-popover:shown`, but not the cancelable `awc-popover:show`.

```js
popover.show();
```

### `hide`

Hides the popover, and the popovers nested in it first. Focus returns to the trigger if it was inside the popover, or
lost. Emits `awc-popover:hidden`, but not the cancelable `awc-popover:hide`.

```js
await popover.hide();
```

### `requestShow`

Shows the popover as if the user asked to. Emits a cancelable `awc-popover:show`, then a cancelable `awc-popover:hide` on
each other open popover except the ones it is nested in. Does nothing if any of them is prevented.

```js
popover.requestShow();
```

### `requestHide`

Hides the popover as if the user asked to. Emits a cancelable `awc-popover:hide` on each popover nested in it,
innermost first, then on the popover itself. Stops at the first one prevented: that popover and the ones it is nested
in stay open, and the ones nested in it that allowed it close. Called again with the same event, it asks no popover a
second time.

```js
await popover.requestHide();
```

### `toggle`

Shows or hides the popover as if its trigger was clicked: calls `requestShow` or `requestHide`. Pass the event that
toggled it, if any, so that a popover the same press already asked to hide isn't asked again.

```js
await popover.toggle();
```

### `reposition`

Updates the position of the popover element. If you are rendering elements lazily within the popover element, you can
call this function to update the popover's placement once the elements have been loaded. Does nothing while the popover
is closed.

```js
await popover.reposition();
```

## Events

Events work as they do on native elements. A user action, or a `requestShow`, `requestHide` or `toggle` call, first
emits a cancelable `show` or `hide`; calling `preventDefault()` on it stops the popover from opening or closing.
`show()`, `hide()` and changing `open` act directly and emit no `show` or `hide`. `shown` and
`hidden` fire after every open and close, whatever caused it. Connecting, moving and removing the element emit nothing.

Like the other events, `show` and `hide` bubble. A listener on an element that contains other popovers receives their
`show` and `hide` too, so check `event.target` before preventing one.

| Name                 | Bubbles | Cancelable | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------               | ------- | ---------- | ------------                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `awc-popover:show`   | `true`  | `true`     | Fires before the popover opens for a user action or `requestShow`. Opening the popover also asks the other open popovers to hide.                                                                                             |
| `awc-popover:shown`  | `true`  | `false`    | Fires after the popover has opened.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `awc-popover:hide`   | `true`  | `true`     | Fires before the popover closes for a user action or `requestHide`: its trigger, a close button, Escape, an outside click, focus moving out of it, another popover opening, or a request to hide the popover it is nested in. |
| `awc-popover:hidden` | `true`  | `false`    | Fires after the popover has closed.                                                                                                                                                                                           |

---

---
url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/hooks/introduction.md
---
# Introduction

Hooks are functions that attach to an [`impulse`](https://github.com/Ambiki/impulse) element while it stays
connected, and clean up after themselves when it disconnects.

## Usage

Call a hook from the element's `connected` lifecycle callback.

In this example, the [`useOutsideClick`](./use-outside-click.md) hook listens for clicks outside the `pop-over` element
and the `#button` element. When the user clicks outside both, the `callback` hides the `pop-over` element by adding the
`hidden` attribute.

```ts
import { ImpulseElement, registerElement } from '@ambiki/impulse';
import { useOutsideClick } from '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/hooks';

@registerElement('pop-over')
export default class PopoverElement extends ImpulseElement {
  connected() {
    useOutsideClick(this, {
      boundaries: [this, document.querySelector('#button')],
      callback: () => {
        if (this.open) {
          this.hidden = true;
        }
      },
    });
  }

  get open() {
    return !this.hasAttribute('hidden');
  }
}
```

---

---
url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/hooks/use-floating-ui.md
---
# useFloatingUI

A thin wrapper around [Floating UI](https://floating-ui.com/) for positioning a floating element, such as a tooltip,
dropdown, or popover, against its anchor.

::: tip `useFloatingUI` or Anchor?
Use this hook when you are writing your own [`impulse`](https://github.com/Ambiki/impulse) element that opens and
closes a floating element. If you only need something positioned from markup, use the
[Anchor](../components/anchor.md) component instead. Both share the same positioning logic and defaults.
:::

## Usage

```ts
import { ImpulseElement, registerElement, target } from '@ambiki/impulse';
import { useFloatingUI } from '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/hooks';

@registerElement('pop-over')
export default class PopoverElement extends ImpulseElement {
  // The anchor.
  @target() button: HTMLButtonElement;

  // The floating element, positioned against the anchor.
  @target() panel: HTMLElement;

  private floatingUI: ReturnType<typeof useFloatingUI>;

  connected() {
    this.floatingUI = useFloatingUI(this, {
      anchorElement: this.button,
      floatingElement: this.panel,
      placement: 'bottom',
    });
  }

  show() {
    // Show the popover.
    this.panel.hidden = false;
    // Start positioning logic.
    this.floatingUI.start();
  }

  async hide() {
    // Hide the popover.
    this.panel.hidden = true;
    // Stop positioning logic.
    await this.floatingUI.stop();
  }

  // Repositioning does nothing while this is `false`.
  get open() {
    return !this.panel.hasAttribute('hidden');
  }
}
```

## Arguments

```ts
useFloatingUI(element, options);
```

### `element`

| Name    | Default | Description                           |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------------------------- |
| element | N/A     | The impulse element (usually `this`), with an `open` property. The hook stops when the element disconnects. |

### `options`

Either an object, or a function that returns one. An object is read once, when the hook is created. A function is
called every time the `floatingElement` is repositioned, so options that change while it's open (such as a `placement`
attribute) are picked up on the next reposition. Call the returned `update()` to reposition straight away.

`start()` keeps following the `anchorElement` and `floatingElement` it found when it was called. If the function
returns different elements later, call `stop()` and then `start()` to follow the new ones.

```ts
this.floatingUI = useFloatingUI(this, () => ({
  anchorElement: this.button,
  floatingElement: this.panel,
  placement: this.placement,
}));
```

| Name            | Default     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| anchorElement   | N/A         | The element (or a virtual element, such as a pointer position) to position against.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| floatingElement | N/A         | The element to position against the `anchorElement`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| arrowElement    | `undefined` | An element inside the `floatingElement` that points at the `anchorElement`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| arrowPadding    | `0`         | The padding in pixels between the arrow and the edges of the `floatingElement`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| middleware      | `[]`        | Array of Floating UI middleware for fine-grained positioning control. They run after the built-in middleware and before the arrow is aligned. Read the [docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/middleware).                                                                                                                               |
| offsetOptions   | `0`         | Adds distance between the `anchorElement` and the `floatingElement`. Read the [docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/offset).                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| placement       | `bottom`    | The preferred placement of the `floatingElement`. The actual placement may vary to keep it inside the viewport. One of `top`, `top-start`, `top-end`, `right`, `right-start`, `right-end`, `bottom`, `bottom-start`, `bottom-end`, `left`, `left-start`, or `left-end`. Read the [docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/tutorial#placements). |
| flipOptions     | `undefined` | Options for flipping the `floatingElement` to another placement when the preferred one doesn't fit. Flipping is always on. Read the [docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/flip).                                                                                                                                                             |
| keepFlipped     | `false`     | Keeps the side the `floatingElement` flipped to until `stop()` is called, instead of trying `placement` first on every reposition, so it doesn't jump back once its content shrinks. It still flips again when that side stops fitting.                                                                                                    |
| shiftOptions    | `undefined` | Options for shifting the `floatingElement` along the `anchorElement` to keep it inside the viewport. Shifting is always on. Read the [docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/shift).                                                                                                                                                           |
| strategy        | `fixed`     | The value of the `position` CSS property. One of `absolute` or `fixed`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| sync            | `undefined` | Matches the `floatingElement`'s size to the `anchorElement`'s. One of `height`, `width`, or `both`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| autoSize        | `undefined` | Exposes the space available to the `floatingElement` as the `--awc-auto-size-height` and `--awc-auto-size-width` CSS custom properties. One of `height`, `width`, or `both`. A `floatingElement` capped to that space flips when it is squashed and the other side has more room.                                                          |
| autoSizePadding | `0`         | The padding in pixels to keep from the viewport edge when measuring the available space.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## Returns

The hook places the `floatingElement` once when it's created. After that, repositioning does nothing while `open` is
`false`. It returns:

| Name       | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start()`  | Starts positioning the `floatingElement`, and keeps it next to the `anchorElement` as the page scrolls or resizes.               |
| `update()` | Repositions the `floatingElement` straight away. Returns a promise. Does nothing while `open` is `false`.                        |
| `stop()`   | Stops positioning. The `floatingElement` stays where it was last placed. Returns a promise that resolves once it has stopped, on the next frame if it was running. |

---

---
url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/hooks/use-focus-out.md
---
# useFocusOut

Listen for focus moving to an element outside the defined `boundaries`, such as on Tab past the last element of a
popover. Use it to close a floating element that keyboard users have left, so it doesn't stay open behind them.

::: tip Pair it with `useOutsideClick`
`useFocusOut` leaves most presses outside to [`useOutsideClick`](./use-outside-click.md). Use both hooks, with the same
`boundaries`, to cover the keyboard and the pointer.
:::

## Usage

```ts
import { ImpulseElement, registerElement, target } from '@ambiki/impulse';
import { useFocusOut, useOutsideClick } from '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/hooks';

@registerElement('pop-over')
export default class PopoverElement extends ImpulseElement {
  // The trigger.
  @target() button: HTMLButtonElement;

  // The floating element.
  @target() panel: HTMLElement;

  connected() {
    const boundaries = [this.button, this.panel];

    // Focus moving outside, such as on Tab past the panel's last element.
    useFocusOut(this, { boundaries, callback: () => this.hide() });

    // A press outside, including one that moves focus to a field outside.
    useOutsideClick(this, { boundaries, callback: () => this.hide() });
  }

  hide() {
    // Both callbacks can run while the panel is hidden, or for the same press.
    if (!this.open) return;
    this.panel.hidden = true;
  }

  get open() {
    return !this.panel.hidden;
  }
}
```

## Arguments

```ts
useFocusOut(element, options);
```

### `element`

| Name    | Default | Description                                                                         |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| element | N/A     | The impulse element (usually `this`). The hook stops listening when it disconnects. |

### `options`

| Name       | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| boundaries | N/A     | An array of HTML elements that focus can move into, or between, without invoking the `callback` function. `null` entries are skipped.                                                                                                                            |
| callback   | N/A     | The function to call when focus moves outside. `event` is the `focusin` event and `target` is the element that received focus, or its shadow host when that element is in a shadow root. Signature: `callback: (event: FocusEvent, target: HTMLElement) => void` |

## What counts as focus moving out

* The `callback` runs on every move to an element outside the `boundaries`, even when focus wasn't inside them before.
  Check your own state first, such as whether the popover is open.
* Focus leaving the page, such as to another tab or window, doesn't count. Neither does focus falling back to `<body>`,
  such as when the focused element is removed.
* Focus moved by a press outside, to the element pressed or the focusable element around it, doesn't count. That press
  is left to `useOutsideClick`.
* A press outside that moves focus somewhere else, such as on a `<label>` that focuses its field, counts as well. Both
  callbacks run for it, so make them safe to run twice.
* Focus moved by a press inside does count, such as a button in the popover that opens a dialog elsewhere on the page.
* Boundaries inside a shadow root aren't supported. Focus moving into a shadow root is seen as a move to its shadow
  host.

---

---
url: https://ambiki.github.io/impulse_view_components/hooks/use-outside-click.md
---
# useOutsideClick

Listen for clicks that occur outside the defined `boundaries`.

A click counts when the press that starts it, with the primary button, lands outside every boundary. A click without a
press, such as from Enter or `click()`, doesn't count, and neither does one prevented before it reaches `document`, such
as by a `window` capture listener.

::: tip Pair it with `useFocusOut`
Keyboard users leave a popover with Tab, not a click. Use [`useFocusOut`](./use-focus-out.md), with the same
`boundaries`, to catch focus moving out.
:::

## Usage

```ts
import { ImpulseElement, registerElement } from '@ambiki/impulse';
import { useOutsideClick } from '@ambiki/impulse-view-components/hooks';

@registerElement('pop-over')
export default class PopoverElement extends ImpulseElement {
  connected() {
    useOutsideClick(this, {
      boundaries: [this, document.querySelector('#button')],
      callback: () => {
        // Only proceed if the popover element is open.
        if (this.open) {
          this.hidden = true;
        }
      },
    });
  }

  get open() {
    return !this.hasAttribute('hidden');
  }
}
```

## Arguments

```ts
useOutsideClick(element, options);
```

### `element`

| Name    | Default   | Description                           |
| ------  | --------- | -------------                         |
| element | N/A       | The impulse element (usually `this`). The hook stops listening when it disconnects. |

### `options`

| Name       | Default   | Description                                                                                                                 |
| ------     | --------- | -------------                                                                                                               |
| boundaries | N/A       | An array of HTML elements that clicks can land in without invoking the `callback` function. `null` entries are skipped. |
| callback   | N/A       | The function to call when an outside click is detected. `event` is the `click` event and `element` is the element the press landed on. Signature: `callback: (event: Event, element: HTMLElement) => void` |
